summary.text: 两 is the standardized simplified form of 兩. It is used for ‘two’, ‘both’ and ‘pair’; early bronze inscriptions also use 兩 for quantities and measures, including a measure associated with horses. The traditional graph’s original construction remains disputed.

formation.text: The traditional graph’s formation is disputed. Shuowen analyzes 兩 as 一 plus 㒳, with 㒳 meaning ‘divide evenly’ and also supplying sound; this is a lexicographic account, not confirmation of the graph’s original construction. Other proposals read the form as a chariot front or as a modified chariot part marking a pair of horses, but neither depiction is established. A proposed analysis as two 丙 forms is also unverified. The modern shape 两 does not resolve these questions.

history.text: 㒳 is reported in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions. A form with an added upper stroke, 兩, appears by the Spring and Autumn period and gradually becomes dominant. The precise graphic continuity between these forms is uncertain.

两 was used as a variant spelling of 兩 before modern standardization and is now its standardized simplified counterpart. The evidence does not show whether a particular historical variant directly supplied the modern standard form.

uncertainties.text: The original graphic analysis remains unsettled: Shuowen’s account and the chariot-front and paired-horse proposals are distinct interpretations, none confirmed as the original depiction. Reported Old Chinese transcriptions make a sound similarity between 丙 and 兩 plausible, but do not establish that 丙 forms the graph’s components.

senses.text: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions attest quantity and measure uses, including a measure associated with pairs of horses. These examples do not securely date the first abstract numeral use.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions; also recorded in Shuowen
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions attest a weight-unit use, and Shuowen defines 兩 as twenty-four zhu. How this sense relates historically to quantity or measure uses is unresolved.
两 is used for ‘both’, ‘pair’ and ‘couple’. The available evidence does not date these meanings or connect them to the early measure uses through a specific transition.
‘Ounce’ is recorded as a gloss for 两/兩, but its historical relation to the earlier weight-unit use is not traced here.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a dated semantic sequence linking the horse-pair measure, numeral ‘two’, ‘both/pair’ and the weight unit.
The historical use and development of the gloss ‘ounce’ are not traced here.

overview.text: 两 is the simplified form of 兩, used for ‘two’, ‘both’ and a pair. Early inscriptions also use 兩 for quantities and measures, including one associated with horses; the original shape remains disputed.

takeaway.text: Chariot-front and paired-horse explanations are proposals, not confirmed pictures of the earliest graph.
